name: QuantumScience Claw
question: Can a local AI agent coordinate quantum error-correction software while preserving scientific correctness, reproducibility, and evidence?
summary: A locally deployed scientific agent for verifiable quantum error-correction workflows.

architecture.detail: Selected MIT ScienceClaw components for registered skills and artifact provenance
QHPC Ecosystem (EQO), typed operations, and approved computational workers
Stim, Sinter, PyMatching, and other supported tools

layers.title: Execution
layers.body: The scientific software runs and produces an artifact.

layers.title: Scientific verification
layers.body: The artifact passes the relevant mathematical or numerical checks.

layers.title: Task completion
layers.body: The agent correctly submits and communicates the verified outcome.

benchmarks: Verified scientific evidence for all 24 tasks
Limited reproduction, not the full external study
Replay within the pinned computational environment
limitations: Benchmark configurations do not expose identical scientific capabilities: QSC has a specialized Stim synthesis operation. Results evaluate the complete system, not the isolated effect of orchestration or verification.
The deterministic synthesis backend can solve the benchmark instances directly; agent completion remains lower, highlighting the gap between tool capability and end-to-end reliability.
One adaptive episode met six precision targets below a 49,152-shot budget. It does not establish better sample efficiency than conventional policies.
A 24-configuration, 1.2-million-shot study failed its prespecified goodness-of-fit criterion, so no threshold estimate was accepted.
Infrastructure detected seven controlled faults. The agent correctly completed failure reporting in two cases, rising to three with more explicit guidance.
Replay reconstructs recorded evidence in a pinned environment; it is not independent replication with different algorithms or implementations.

latency.note: Different denominators: these medians are not an additive end-to-end time breakdown.

publication: Research in progress. Evaluation results describe the current system.
